title: "Hook Templates and CI"

# Hook Templates: Sharing Hooks Across Repos

After this page you can point new repos at a shared hooks directory, and you know why CI still has to run on the server.

## `.git/hooks` is local

Cloning does **not** copy hooks (Git ignores them in the payload on purpose: a clone would otherwise execute someone else’s scripts). Each clone needs its own install step.

## `core.hooksPath`

```bash
mkdir -p ~/desk/git-hooks
# put pre-commit, commit-msg, … there, chmod +x
git config --global core.hooksPath ~/desk/git-hooks
```

Every repo on this Linux user account now runs those hooks. A repo can override with `git config core.hooksPath .githooks` (a directory **inside** the project that you *do* commit).

Project-local, committed:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/desk/desk-api/.githooks
# copy scripts, chmod +x, commit them
git config core.hooksPath .githooks
```

New clones still must run the `git config` once, or a `Makefile` / `just` recipe / `bin/install-hooks` script. Document that in `README.md`.

## `init.templateDir`

```bash
mkdir -p ~/desk/git-template/hooks
# scripts in that hooks dir
git config --global init.templateDir ~/desk/git-template
```

`git init` and `git clone` copy the template’s `hooks/` into the new `.git/hooks`. Good for your laptop. Teammates need the same config.

## CI is the hook you cannot skip

A `pre-commit` hook is a courtesy. `git commit --no-verify` and a forge’s web editor skip it. **CI on the forge** (chapter 32, GitHub Actions in Part VI) runs on the server after push. Put the same checks there: `git diff --check`, tests, secret scanning.

```text
 laptop                         forge
 .git/hooks/pre-commit          pre-receive / CI job
    │ skippable                    │ not skippable
    ▼                              ▼
 git commit                     git push accepted
    │                              │
    └──────── git push ────────────┘
```

Client hooks catch mistakes in milliseconds on Linux. CI is the policy. Use both.

## Frameworks

[pre-commit.com](https://pre-commit.com) is a Python manager that installs a tiny `.git/hooks/pre-commit` and runs a YAML list of linters. Optional. Raw bash hooks in this chapter teach the mechanism; a framework is fine in production if the team already uses it.
